state:
I don't usually write long reviews but this trip had a lot going on so bear with me. We stayed at the Palm Court Resort for a full week, June 9th through June 16th, to celebrate my parents' 40th anniversary, so there were nine of us total across three connecting rooms on the 4th floor, facing the courtyard side rather than the ocean side since we booked kind of late and the ocean rooms were sold out by then. Check-in itself was smooth, the woman at the front desk, I think her name tag said Priya, upgraded my parents' room to a small balcony suite for free when she found out about the anniversary, which was such a sweet gesture and honestly set a great tone for the whole week.

The pool area is gorgeous, there are two pools actually, a quieter adults-only one and a bigger family one with a small water slide for the kids, my nephews were in there for hours every single day and never got bored. The breakfast buffet included in our rate was surprisingly good for a resort of this size, fresh omelet station, real scrambled eggs, decent coffee, though by day 5 we were all a little tired of the same pastry selection, minor thing though.

Now here's the part I actually want other travelers to know before booking. On the fourth night, June 12th, the air conditioning in our specific room (412) completely stopped working around 11pm. We called the front desk, they sent an engineer within maybe 20 minutes who confirmed the compressor unit for that room had failed and said it would need a part they didn't have on site. They moved us to a different room, 438, for that night and the compressor was fixed by the next afternoon, June 13th, so we moved back in. Total inconvenience but they handled it about as well as they could have, and comped us a $50 dining credit for the trouble without us even asking, which I thought was a nice touch.

Separately, on the sixth night, June 14th, there was a wedding reception happening in the ballroom two floors below us that ran until around 1am with a live band, and honestly the bass was audible in our room even with the AC (the fixed one) running to create white noise. We didn't call about it because it ended reasonably by 1am and we figured it's a resort, weddings happen. I want to be clear though that this was ONLY that one night, June 14th - the rest of the week, including the other nights after the AC was fixed, was completely quiet, no other noise issues at all.

Oh, and totally separate from our stay, my sister-in-law's family did a similar trip last year but stayed at a completely different chain, some Coastline Suites property two towns over, and she said THEIR room had a mold smell in the bathroom the whole week that housekeeping never resolved despite three requests - glad that wasn't us, and again, different hotel entirely.

Checkout was easy, final bill matched what we expected including the $50 credit applied correctly, no surprise charges. Would absolutely stay here again and already looking at dates for next year. The only real critique, if I'm forced to give one, is maybe rotate the breakfast pastries more after day 4 or 5.

A couple more small things since I'm already this deep into a review: the resort shuttle to the nearby outlet mall ran every 30 minutes as posted and was never late in the four times we used it, and the in-room mini fridge in 412 and 438 both worked fine even during the AC swap, so nothing in there spoiled. My father, who is admittedly picky about mattresses, said the bed was the most comfortable he's had at any resort we've been to as a family, which is saying something since we've done a lot of these anniversary trips over the years. Wifi worked everywhere we tried it, lobby, pool, and both room configurations, no dead zones that we noticed, which isn't always a given at older resort properties like this one.

state:
Been a Gold member of the Meridian Hotels loyalty program for 3 years, staying here on business roughly twice a month. This particular stay at the Meridian Uptown, Sept 18-20 (2 nights), had a few issues worth documenting.

First, the rate: I booked through the app at the 'member rate' of $189/night, confirmation email confirmed $189/night x 2 nights = $378 plus tax. Final folio at checkout showed $214/night x 2 = $428 plus tax, a $50 total discrepancy. I brought this to the front desk, who couldn't explain it and forwarded me to reservations. Reservations emailed back the next day: "We've reviewed your booking and confirmed a rate-loading error affected member-rate bookings made between Sept 15-17 for this property; you were charged the standard rate instead of your member rate. We've corrected this and refunded the $50 difference to your card, which should post within 3-5 business days." That's a relief, though it took four emails back and forth over five days to get there.

Second, and separately, my Gold tier benefits weren't honored at check-in: no room upgrade offer (not guaranteed, I know), and worse, the welcome amenity (a bottle of water and snack, standard for Gold members) never appeared in the room either time I checked (day 1 and day 2). I mentioned it to the front desk on day 2 and they apologized and sent up the amenity within the hour, so at least day 2 was resolved, day 1 was just missed entirely with no compensation offered for that specific miss.

Third, on an unrelated note, my colleague Ravi who was traveling with me but booked his own separate reservation (not part of my booking) had zero issues at all - correct rate charged, amenity delivered same-day both days, upgraded to a corner room without even asking. Just goes to show it might have been specific to my reservation's rate-loading bug rather than a property-wide issue, since his booking window was outside Sept 15-17 (he booked in August).

Room itself, when I actually look at just the room: clean, quiet, comfortable bed, no complaints there at all. Gym was well-equipped, open 24 hours as advertised. Would still stay here again given it's convenient for my client meetings nearby, but wanted to document the billing issue in case others from this booking window see the same discrepancy and think they're just being overcharged with no explanation.

One last thing: I saw another review on this site from someone claiming the pool was closed their entire visit - that was not the case during my stay, the pool was open and honestly lovely both mornings I used it.
